hops.note:
coverage_check.py's own DUMP_DIR dict hardcodes six providers -- digitalocean was not in it, so write-artifacts.md's own core command failed outright with "unknown provider" before anything could be recomputed. Fixed by adding the entry (ubiquex-docs, pending commit). Once unblocked, the real coverage report (849 total gaps: 196 missing intro, 59 missing category, 398 missing depth-0 field description) surfaced a much bigger, real problem: DigitalOcean's own resource-reference SERVICE grouping is mechanically wrong, not a content gap. ir.go's ServiceAndLocalName takes wire_type's own second token as service (RealNamespace, the real fix already built for exactly this class of problem for AWS via CFN's own namespace field, is empty for every openapi-sourced provider -- deliberately, per mergegroup.go's own doc comment: 'openapi and discoverydoc both emit a real, honest empty map... already correct by construction,' true for Kubernetes/GitHub/Datadog/Azure's own wire-naming conventions, false for DigitalOcean's). Real, live-confirmed effect: nearly all 59 resources landed in their own single-resource service (load, floating, reserved, db, database, cluster, pool, replica, config...) instead of DigitalOcean's real product taxonomy. Separately, two wire names (digitalocean_byoip_prefixe, digitalocean_registrie) look like the same singularization bug UBI-102 already found and fixed for GCP.

Confirmed a real, clean fix source exists before writing any code: DigitalOcean's own real spec carries genuine, human-authored operation tags (Load Balancers, Droplets, VPCs, Kubernetes, Container Registry, SSH Keys -- read directly from the real bundled spec, not assumed) that map exactly onto its real product taxonomy, and resourcemap.Resource/DataSourceCandidate already carry a live *openapi3.Operation with its own real .Tags -- MergeOpenAPIGroup (snapshot package) already surfaces this via embedding, so the real fix is reading it in namespacesForSource's own SchemaSourceOpenAPI case, not new plumbing. Scoped as a new opt-in config flag (mirroring redocly_bundle's own exact precedent) rather than an unconditional change, since switching all openapi-sourced namespaces to tag-based derivation could regress four already-published, live providers (Kubernetes/GitHub/Datadog/Azure) whose current mechanical grouping already happens to be correct -- not attempted yet, stopped to ask the founder before proceeding, per explicit instruction.

While investigating this, found a second, separate, more serious problem: UBI-217's own redocly_bundle fix (previously reported resolved this same session, cited as resolved_by in the loader-check hop above) was NEVER actually merged into ubx-provider-dynamic's real main, or into any tagged release including the currently-published v1.0.2 -- confirmed directly, config.go on both main and v1.0.2 carries zero RedoclyBundle references. Root cause: PR #42 (the redocly_bundle PR) was a real, live instance of TRAPS.md's own 'a stacked PR is only safe while its base is unmerged' trap -- its own base branch (roozbeh/ubi-217-linode-json-surrogate-pair) had already been merged into main by an earlier PR (#41) before #42 itself merged, so #42's real, valid, signed content landed on an already-consumed branch, never on main. The content itself was never lost (confirmed still present, real, signed, at commit fe6efaa on that branch), just never actually integrated. This is why DigitalOcean's own onboarding this session never actually exercised the redocly_bundle code path live -- every real ubx sdk gen call this session resolved the already-pinned v1.0.0 snapshot, whose RawSpec was bundled once already; nothing re-triggered live bundling to notice the fix was missing from main until this investigation needed the real config.go content directly. Fixed: opened https://github.com/Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic/pull/44 (open, not merged, targets the real main with the exact same already-reviewed content).

UBI-222 follow-up (namespace_from_tags): the tag-based namespace fix landed (ubx-provider-dynamic v1.0.5, real fixes across PRs #47/#48/#49 -- the opt-in flag itself, a live non-determinism bug in its own collision resolution, and a live invalid-Go-identifier bug for a tag starting with a digit, both found by actually running this fix against DigitalOcean's real spec end-to-end, not in review). ubx-schema-digitalocean regenerated (v1.0.1, PRs #1/#2) and released; ubiquex re-pinned to 1.0.1 and verified zero-network. ubiquex-docs coverage_check.py's own provider allowlist fixed (PR #58). Real effect: 172 of 195 types now resolve to 43 real, taxonomy-matching namespaces (databases, blockstorage, droplets, kubernetes, byoipprefixes, containerregistries, ...), down from roughly 55 fragmented near-single-resource services. coverage_check.py now runs cleanly against digitalocean: 846 real gaps (196 missing intro, 59 missing category, 397 missing depth-0 field description, 195 pages not yet generated) -- this hop is unblocked, not yet done; the actual content authoring is real, substantial batch work not attempted this turn.

real_gaps_found: coverage_check.py (and, unverified but likely by the same pattern, gen_provider_docs.py/regen_pages.py/corpus_index.py/build_categories.py/check_duplicate_wires.py) hardcode a six-provider allowlist -- none of the three runbooks mention that a genuinely new provider needs adding to these before ANYTHING downstream of the schema pin works at all.

No runbook step verifies real service/namespace grouping quality before artifact-authoring begins -- a provider whose wire-naming convention does not cleanly split into <provider>_<service>_<noun> (true for DigitalOcean, and structurally possible for any future non-Terraform-style REST API) will silently fragment into near-meaningless single-resource service groups, discovered only by actually looking at the real coverage report's own resource list, not by anything the runbook currently tells a session to check.
